title: CIS 560 Exam 1 Preparation and Cheat-Sheet Build
goal: Prepare Adam for the CIS 560 midterm on Thursday, October 22, 2026 by using current-semester instructor authority, homework/class-example problem families, durable behavioral evidence, and the one-US-Letter-page double-sided cheat sheet. Optimize for Xu's announced exam architecture: broad Q1 True/False protection plus four short Q2-Q5 construction/proof problems. Respect the MILCOM and MTH 602 blackout windows, preserve uncertainty until remaining lectures/review are sourced, and require independent transfer before claiming exam readiness.
acceptance_criteria: The October 8 direct instructor exam invariants remain the primary current-semester format authority until transcript/review evidence corrects them.

The full Q2-Q5 candidate-family pool named by Xu is preserved explicitly: simple DFA, simple NFA, regular-expression work, CFG design, PDA design, show RL pumping property, show CFL pumping property, prove not regular with pumping, and prove not context free with CFL pumping.
No future executor collapses the candidate-family pool into a claim that all named types will appear; there are only four Q2-Q5 slots and exact selection remains unknown.
Q1 preparation protects broad definitions, distinctions, theorem directionality, closure facts, machine-power comparisons, common traps, and explicit exclusions through rapid T/F-style practice.
Q2-Q5 preparation is driven by independent closed-book redos of homework/class examples plus nearby variants, written in compact 75-minute-exam form rather than homework-length exposition.

Pumping-property questions are practiced as partition plus three conditions; nonregular/non-CFL pumping proofs are practiced with p-dependent witness plus all legal split/placement cases plus contradiction.
The study plan does not rely on CIS 560 work during MILCOM October 11-15 or the MTH 602 study block October 16-19 morning.
HW3 completion is used as study context but not as automatic mastery evidence; guided HW3 skills receive fresh cold-transfer checks before promotion.

The cheat sheet remains a living two-sided US Letter artifact organized around Q1 T/F protection and Q2-Q5 execution recipes, with no long prose and no final density freeze before Xu's October 20 review.
CYK is protected as conceptually exam-relevant required reading; Lecture 11 transcript explicitly says the complete CYK procedure will not be tested.

Current explicit exclusions remain protected: full CFG-to-CNF conversion procedure is not an exam requirement; proofs of Lemmas 2.21 and 2.27 are not required; Lecture 12 explicitly excludes Section 2.4.
Historical 2019 syllabus/homework/student cheat-sheet evidence may predict stable problem families but never overrides current-semester Xu guidance.

Lecture 11 transcript and Lecture 12 instructor notes are durably ingested and have reweighted scope; a genuine Lecture 12 transcript remains optional source recovery if available, and the October 20 review remains the strongest final weighting event.
By exam day, high-relevance pillar skills have delayed/fresh behavioral evidence sufficient for exam-ready claims, and unresolved secondary material is at least safely protected on the cheat sheet.
